title: Infinitely many negative-energy weak solutions of a degenerate fractional p-Kirchhoff system with singular and critical nonlinearities
author: Mohamed Louchaich
work: Multiple solutions for Kirchhoff type systems involving singular and critical nonlinearities
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026, No. 05, pp. 1--18; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.05; publisher version
difficulty_reason: After the fractional Sobolev embedding, the Brezis-Lieb splitting, the Krasnoselskii genus and Kajikiya symmetric mountain pass lemma and the Palais-Smale theory for the approximating problem are supplied, the counted theorem still needs a source-local passage from the critical points of the perturbed problem to the singular original system. The author must bound the whole approximating family uniformly through the degenerate Kirchhoff function, extract the weak limit together with the concentration pair of equation (4.13), force the critical-term deficit eta to vanish by a two-level energy comparison at exponents sigma < sigma_0 with p sigma_0 below the fractional critical exponent, and then run a separate zero-tension case. This degenerate fractional singular-to-critical compactness mechanism is research level, not a qualification exercise.
